components.css: .ds-tags{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px} .ds-tag{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;height:26px;padding:0 10px 0 9px;border:1px solid var(--rule, #e2dccf);border-radius:6px;background:var(--card, #fffdf8);color:var(--ink, #22201b);font:500 0.8rem/1 "IBM Plex Sans", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;text-decoration:none;white-space:nowrap;transition:border-color .15s,box-shadow .15s} .ds-tag::before{content:"";width:8px;height:8px;box-sizing:border-box;border:1.5px solid var(--c);border-radius:50%} .ds-tag.ds-theory::before{border-radius:1.5px} .ds-tag.ds-formalized{border-color:color-mix(in oklab,var(--c) 45%,var(--rule, #e2dccf));background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--c) 11%,var(--card, #fffdf8))} .ds-tag.ds-formalized::before{background:var(--c)} .ds-tag.ds-progress::before{background:linear-gradient(90deg,var(--c) 50%,transparent 50%)} .ds-tag:hover{border-color:var(--c)} .ds-tag.ds-sel{border-color:var(--ink, #22201b);box-shadow:0 0 0 1.5px var(--ink, #22201b)} .ds-tag.ds-in{box-shadow:0 0 0 1.5px var(--amber, #c2700c)} .ds-tag:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus, #2563eb);outline-offset:2px}

components.css: .ds-chips{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:5px} .ds-chip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;height:26px;padding:0 4px 0 10px;border:1px solid var(--rule, #e2dccf);border-radius:6px;background:var(--card, #fffdf8);color:var(--ink, #22201b);font:500 0.8rem "IBM Plex Sans", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif;cursor:pointer} .ds-chip:hover{border-color:var(--ink-3, #6b665e)} .ds-chip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus, #2563eb);outline-offset:2px} .ds-n{min-width:18px;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--ink, #22201b) 8%,transparent);color:var(--ink-2, #4f4b44);font-size:.72rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums} .ds-chip.ds-more{padding:0 10px;border-style:dashed;color:var(--ink-3, #6b665e)}

narrative.overview:
The site is a map of a field. Each hub of the collection is a region with its own colour, and every name on the map leads somewhere: a paper to what it cites, an author to their co-authors and institutions, a venue to its authors. The notes stay quiet beside the map. The interface is ink on archive paper by day and the same ink, lightened, on a green-black forest night: little text, small type, hairlines, and colour spent only where it carries information.

One visual language runs through every view, list, chip and card. Colour is the hub. Shape is the kind of paper: round for a method, square for theory. Fill is the status: solid once formalized, half while in progress, dotted when partly covered, hollow to do. What an entry cites is drawn in ink, what cites it in amber. A reader who learns these four encodings once can read the tree, the timeline, the graphs and the lists without a legend.

The density is that of a well-set reference work: compact, labelled, legible at a glance and in bulk. Nothing is raised, glowing or ornamental; the data carries the colour, and the chrome stays paper and ink.
keyCharacteristics: Warm archive paper and iron-gall ink by day; forest night by dark, chosen by the reader or the system.
Hub colour as the only categorical colour; citation amber as the only directional one.
Serif for what a thing is called, sans for everything that describes or labels it.
Flat tonal layering; one soft shadow, for what floats under the pointer.
Small tags and pills for collections; plain text links for reading (bylines, citations).

rules.name: The Hub Owns the Colour Rule
rules.body: Categorical colour belongs to the hubs. Interface chrome (tabs, buttons, panels, links) stays paper and ink; no hue is spent on decoration.

rules.name: The Two Directions Rule
rules.body: Ink for what an entry cites, amber for what cites it. Amber is never a highlight, a warning or an accent elsewhere.

rules.name: The Faint Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Ink Faint marks structure (an underline, a "·", a section dash). Any word, count or year is Ink Muted at the lightest.

rules.name: The Serif Names Things Rule
rules.body: Literata only for what a thing is called or counted; never for a label, a control or running metadata.

rules.name: The Small-Caps Labels Rule
rules.body: A section is introduced by a short uppercase label with a faint dash before it, never by a heading of larger size; the content carries the weight.

rules.name: The Readable Width Rule
rules.body: No line of related text spans the full stage; cap it so the eye can travel from a name to its date.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Everything at rest lies flat on the paper. Only what floats above the pointer casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Mark Grammar Rule
rules.body: Round is a method, square is theory; solid is formalized, half is in progress, dotted is partly covered, hollow is to do. These shapes and fills mean nothing else anywhere on the site.

dos: Do spend colour only on hubs (hub colours) and on the direction of a citation (ink, amber).
Do keep the mark grammar everywhere an entry appears: hub colour, shape for the kind, fill for the status.
Do use Literata for names, titles and figures, and IBM Plex Sans for everything else.
Do separate rows by spacing (5–7px gaps) and cap text width inside full-width panels.
Do give every name in a panel a link to its own panel.
donts: Don't draw a rule between every row of a list or byline; the user rejected rows of horizontal bars.
Don't set a byline or a citation as pills; pills are for collections the reader browses and jumps through.
Don't use amber for anything but what cites an entry.
Don't add shadows to panels, tags or chips at rest.
Don't set words in Ink Faint.
